Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Jasmeet Singh
 Order

This is an application seeking bail in FIR No. 10/2022 dated 12.11.2022, under Sections 13(1) (c)
(a) and 13(2) Prevention of Corruption Act read with Sections 409/420/120-B IPC, registered at Police Station- ACB/New Delhi.
2. The applicant is the CFO of Aurrum e-pay.

The FIR has been registered by Delhi Jal Board which had awarded the work of setting up of automative bill payment collection machines at different locations in different DJB offices for facilitating consumers to make bill payments.
The contract was given to Corporation Bank and was extended from time to time.
The Corporation Bank entered into a contract based work to M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions which in turn further sub contracted the work to Aurrum E- Payment Pvt. Ltd.

It is stated in the FIR that DJB funds to the tune of more than Rs.
20 crores have been embezzled.

3. Mr Singh, learned counsel appears on behalf of the applicant and states that the erstwhile Corporation Bank (now Union Bank) has filed an application before the DRT for recovery of 5.75 crores against M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions only.
He states that a bare perusal of the status report would show that in the present case over the years, Aurrum has deposited about 466 crores collected from the kiosk.
The applicant was only an employee and there is no allegation of embezzlement against the applicant.
He further states that at best it is recovery proceedings and filing of FIR cannot be used for recovery of monies.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has filed a status report.
The newly impleaded respondent No.2-Delhi Jal Board is supporting the stand of respondent No.1.
6. Since the Delhi Jal Board is supporting the stand of the respondent No.1 there is no need for Delhi Jal Board to file a reply.
7. The Corporation Bank has filed recovery proceedings against M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions only and not against the applicant.
The fact whether the amounts are due and payable by the applicant or Aurrum or M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions can only be adjudicated at the stage of trial.
It is also clear that the applicant was only an employee of Aurrum.
The applicant is not the decision maker and only acts on instructions of the Director of Aurrum.
As regards the dishonest intention, if any, on the part of the applicant can only be inferred after the parties have led evidence and not at the stage of bail.
Prima facie, the fact that Rs. 466 crores collected from the kiosk have been deposited further fortifies the absence of dishonest intention on the part of the applicant.
Moreover, the applicant had resigned from the company in September, 2020 which was prior to the registration of FIR.
9. This order is also passed only for the purposes of adjudicating the bail application and is without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties.
10. The application is disposed of accordingly.
